items.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: I started taking lessons from Herb Sanford, he was one of my teachers.

ctx.x: Well they added to it with quarters and subsistence I think it amounted to around oh I think around $87 or $92 a month or something like that. But see in 1942 for crying out loud, what was the rent? People were paying — oh heck they weren’t paying very much rent. Because you had price and wage controls. So that was to prevent gouging. And so I think I was living with my in-laws but then when I got the apartment I think it was — was it $27.50 a month? Something like that. For a one bedroom duplex. So anyhow we…
